correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge1\), the second-difference map is an injective \(n\) to \(n+2\) matrix and its range equals the codimension-two moment-zero subspace. Orthogonal projection of the hinge representative gives the exact norm; explicit two-by-two Gram inverse produces \(G_{n,j}\). The exact signed consecutive difference shows all and only center maxima. Equality follows from sharp Cauchy–Schwarz, and the rational odd/even formulas give the \(n^{3/2}\) limit. Independent fraction-arithmetic checker inverted \(D^*D\) and verified all site profiles, splines, moments, parities and difference formulas for \(1\le n\le17\) (938 assertions); finite tests are supplementary only.

value.rationale: The natural next Hilbert endpoint for zero-extended second differences is a full finite-length \(\ell^\infty\) norm, not an arbitrary sample. The exact Green diagonal, parity-dependent number of norming sites and explicit cubic extremal splines solve its sharp evaluation classification at all lengths. The limiting constant \(1/(8\sqrt3)\) links discrete beam scaling to continuous second-order Sobolev embeddings; the characterization is a reusable sharp inequality for finite-difference analysis.
